sections.title: Policy and access to the centre
sections.text: Quakenbrück is a small town in Lower Saxony, and the parking policy we could find is thin: the town's own website was not readable (its certificate belongs to another host), so this briefing rests on the Samtgemeinde Artland, which administers the town, the hospital and Deutsche Bahn. The Samtgemeinde's tourism page says more than 500 inner-city parking spaces can be used free of charge, including the large Neuer Markt car park, and separately lists short-stay spaces along Lange Straße, customer spaces in front of shops, disabled spaces and parking at the railway station and the Artland Arena [0]. We found no fee ordinance, council decision or resident-parking rules. A news item of 21 October 2026 announces that the moobil+ bus line M07 will call at two stops in Menslage, a neighbouring municipality, every two hours between 8:00 and 18:00, presented as another way to reach Quakenbrück without a car; the year of the start date is not stated and the timetable was still to be announced [9].

sections.title: Parking developments
sections.text: The developments are about alternatives to the car. A MOIN+ mobility station at the railway station has a secured bicycle station of 40 spaces, a repair station and a new bus shelter, funded by the federal transport ministry; bike spaces cost 1 euro a day, 5 a month or 50 a year [6]. Since 1 July 2024, under the MOIN+ pilot, ten electric cars operated by stadtteilauto Osnabrück were added at ten sites in the district, two of them in Quakenbrück, one at the station and one at the Park der deutschen Einheit [7]. The Samtgemeinde's undated charging list names three e-car charging stations, at the BIQ business park, at the Edeka store and at the Marktplatz, and may be out of date [8]. The DB station page lists bicycle spaces, car parking and a taxi rank, but no number of car spaces or tariff [5].

sections.title: Operators, positioning and utilisation
sections.text:
The only paid car parks we could source are the hospital's. The Christliches Krankenhaus Quakenbrück says its car parks are paid, with the first 30 minutes free, then 1 euro an hour and a daily maximum of 10 euros [1], operated by Osnabrücker Parkstätten Betriebsgesellschaft [2]. Car park P1 is reserved for staff from 05:00 to 14:00, with visitors asked to use P2 in that time, and general visiting hours are daily from 14:00 to 19:00 [3]. The hospital lists disabled parking at its main entrance and says travellers arrive by train via Oldenburg or Osnabrück or by car via the A1 and B68 [4].

Our data cover those two hospital car parks, P1 (183 spaces) and P2 (362), measured for about 60 days since 22 August 2026. Occupancy averaged about 53% on weekdays, weighted by spaces. P2, the visitors' car park, averaged 66% on weekdays and 59% at weekends and reached full in single readings, late on a Saturday night among others. P1, the staff car park, averaged 28% on weekdays and 9% at weekends, but reached full once late on a Wednesday evening. The free inner-city spaces are not in our data. The window includes the end of the summer holidays.
